steps.name: environment - persist non-sensitive env, secure secrets, optional supabase-cli
steps.description: Persist minimal non-sensitive environment variables system-wide under /etc/profile.d and store sensitive secrets in a root-only file (/root/.postgres_secrets, mode 600) that is NOT exported globally. Verify presence and versions of required PostgreSQL tools (psql, pg_dump, pg_restore, pg_isready). Optionally install supabase CLI when SUPABASE_INSTALL=true; verify installed supabase --version and fail if below a minimum recommended version. Ensure npm global bin is exported correctly to PATH in /etc/profile.d if supabase CLI is installed. All operations non-interactive and idempotent. Uses workspace /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/pricecompare-pro-327749/postgresql_db.
steps.script_code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/pricecompare-pro-327749/postgresql_db"
: "${POSTGRES_USER:=devuser}"
: "${POSTGRES_DB:=devdb}"
: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:=devpass}"
: "${SUPABASE_URL:=}"
: "${SUPABASE_KEY:=}"
: "${SUPABASE_INSTALL:=false}"
: "${MIN_SUPABASE_CLI_VER:=1.70.0}"
# Ensure workspace exists with restrictive perms
umask 0077 && mkdir -p "$WORKSPACE"
# Verify required binaries and record versions
for b in psql pg_dump pg_restore pg_isready; do command -v "$b" >/dev/null || { echo "$b not found" >&2; exit 2; }; done
psql --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
pg_dump --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
pg_restore --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
pg_isready --version >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
# Write non-sensitive env to /etc/profile.d
sudo mkdir -p /etc/profile.d
sudo tee /etc/profile.d/postgres_env.sh >/dev/null <<EOF
export POSTGRES_USER="${POSTGRES_USER}"
export POSTGRES_DB="${POSTGRES_DB}"
export SUPABASE_URL="${SUPABASE_URL}"
export POSTGRES_APP_USER="${POSTGRES_USER}"
EOF
sudo chown root:root /etc/profile.d/postgres_env.sh && sudo chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/postgres_env.sh
# Store secrets in root-only file (not exported globally)
if [ -n "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}" ] || [ -n "${SUPABASE_KEY}" ]; then
  sudo tee /root/.postgres_secrets >/dev/null <<EOF
POSTGRES_PASSWORD='${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}'
SUPABASE_KEY='${SUPABASE_KEY}'
EOF
  sudo chown root:root /root/.postgres_secrets && sudo chmod 600 /root/.postgres_secrets
fi
# Optional supabase CLI install (non-interactive). Prefer verifying version after install.
if [ "${SUPABASE_INSTALL}" = "true" ]; then
  command -v npm >/dev/null || { echo "npm required for supabase install" >&2; exit 3; }
  if ! command -v supabase >/dev/null 2>&1; then
    sudo npm i -g supabase --no-audit --no-fund --silent || { echo "supabase npm install failed" >&2; exit 4; }
  fi
  # ensure npm global bin is exported correctly
  NPM_GLOB_BIN=$(npm bin -g 2>/dev/null || true)
  if [ -n "$NPM_GLOB_BIN" ]; then
    sudo tee /etc/profile.d/supabase_path.sh >/dev/null <<'EOF'
# Added by env-01: ensure npm global bin is on PATH for future shells
export PATH="$NPM_GLOB_BIN":\$PATH
EOF
    sudo chown root:root /etc/profile.d/supabase_path.sh && sudo chmod 644 /etc/profile.d/supabase_path.sh
  fi
  # verify supabase CLI version
  if ! command -v supabase >/dev/null 2>&1; then echo "supabase not available after install" >&2; exit 5; fi
  SUP_VER=$(supabase --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $NF}' || true)
  if [ -n "$SUP_VER" ]; then
    # basic semver compare (major.minor.patch) - fail only if obviously older
    if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$MIN_SUPABASE_CLI_VER" "$SUP_VER" | sort -V | head -n1)" != "$MIN_SUPABASE_CLI_VER" ]; then
      echo "supabase CLI version $SUP_VER is older than recommended $MIN_SUPABASE_CLI_VER" >&2; exit 6
    fi
  fi
fi

#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/pricecompare-pro-327749/postgresql_db"
MIGRATIONS="$WORKSPACE/migrations"
SCRIPTS="$WORKSPACE/scripts"
umask 0077 && mkdir -p "$MIGRATIONS" "$SCRIPTS"
# initial migration
MIGRATION_FILE="$MIGRATIONS/0001_init.sql"
if [ ! -f "$MIGRATION_FILE" ]; then
  cat > "$MIGRATION_FILE" <<'SQL'
-- initial migration: create application schema and sample table
CREATE SCHEMA IF NOT EXISTS app_schema;
CREATE TABLE IF NOT EXISTS app_schema.example (
  id serial PRIMARY KEY,
  created_at timestamptz NOT NULL DEFAULT now()
);
SQL
  sudo chmod 600 "$MIGRATION_FILE" || true
fi
# healthcheck script
cat > "$SCRIPTS/healthcheck.sh" <<'BASH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${PGHOST:=localhost}"
: "${PGPORT:=5432}"
: "${POSTGRES_USER:=devuser}"
: "${POSTGRES_DB:=devdb}"
# Source secrets if present
if [ -f /root/.postgres_secrets ]; then source /root/.postgres_secrets; fi
pg_isready -h "$PGHOST" -p "$PGPORT" >/dev/null || { echo "not ready" >&2; exit 2; }
export PGPASSWORD="${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:-}"
psql -h "$PGHOST" -p "$PGPORT" -U "${POSTGRES_USER}" -d "${POSTGRES_DB}" -c "SELECT 1;" -t -A
BASH
sudo chmod 700 "$SCRIPTS/healthcheck.sh" || true
# run_migrations: run sorted migrations and abort on first failure
cat > "$SCRIPTS/run_migrations.sh" <<'BASH'
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="${WORKSPACE}"
: "${POSTGRES_DB:=devdb}"
# Source secrets for PGPASSWORD
if [ -f /root/.postgres_secrets ]; then source /root/.postgres_secrets; fi
pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432 >/dev/null || { echo "postgres not ready" >&2; exit 2; }
shopt -s nullglob
for f in "${WORKSPACE}"/migrations/*.sql; do
  [ -f "$f" ] || continue
  sudo -u postgres psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d "${POSTGRES_DB}" -f "$f" || { echo "migration failed: $f" >&2; exit 3; }
done
BASH
sudo chmod 700 "$SCRIPTS/run_migrations.sh" || true
# README
README="$WORKSPACE/README.md"
if [ ! -f "$README" ]; then
  cat > "$README" <<MD
# postgresql_db workspace
- Workspace: /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/pricecompare-pro-327749/postgresql_db
- Migrations: migrations/*.sql (permissions 600)
- Scripts: scripts/healthcheck.sh (700) scripts/run_migrations.sh (700)

  sudo chmod 644 "$README" || true
fi

steps.name: configuration - create DB, application role and apply grants idempotently
steps.description: Idempotently create the target database and an application role POSTGRES_APP_USER (defaults to POSTGRES_USER). Validate POSTGRES_APP_USER against a safe regex, safely quote and escape database name, set the password securely by passing it to psql via a psql variable or using format(%L) inside a DO block but avoid direct unsafe shell expansion. Use sudo -u postgres for privileged operations. Invoke workspace/scripts/run_migrations.sh to apply all migrations. Ensure pg_isready before DB actions. Uses workspace /home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/pricecompare-pro-327749/postgresql_db.

output_scripts.name: configuration
output_scripts.code:
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
: "${POSTGRES_USER:=devuser}"
: "${POSTGRES_APP_USER:=${POSTGRES_USER}}"
: "${POSTGRES_DB:=devdb}"
: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:=devpass}"
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/pricecompare-pro-327749/postgresql_db"
# Validate app user
if ! [[ "${POSTGRES_APP_USER}" =~ ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,63}$ ]]; then
  echo "invalid POSTGRES_APP_USER: must match ^[a-z0-9_-]{1,63}$" >&2; exit 2
fi
# Ensure postgres ready
pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432 >/dev/null || { echo "postgres not ready" >&2; exit 3; }
# Escape DB name for SQL (double single-quotes)
SAFE_DB=$(printf '%s' "$POSTGRES_DB" | sed "s/'/''/g")
# Create database if missing (robust quoting)
if ! sudo -u postgres psql -tAc "SELECT 1 FROM pg_database WHERE datname = '${SAFE_DB}'" | grep -q 1; then
  sudo -u postgres psql -c "CREATE DATABASE \"${POSTGRES_DB}\";" || { echo "create database failed" >&2; exit 4; }
fi
# Load secrets file if present (not exported globally)
if [ -f /root/.postgres_secrets ]; then
  # shellcheck disable=SC1090
  source /root/.postgres_secrets
fi
# Use POSTGRES_PASSWORD (possibly from secrets file) for role creation
PGPW="${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
# Create or alter role securely using psql variables and format(...%L)
sudo -u postgres psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -v app_user="${POSTGRES_APP_USER}" -v pw="${PGPW}" <<'SQL' || { echo "create/alter role failed" >&2; exit 5; }
DO $$
BEGIN
  IF NOT EXISTS (SELECT FROM pg_catalog.pg_roles WHERE rolname = :'app_user') THEN
    EXECUTE format('CREATE ROLE %I LOGIN PASSWORD %L', :'app_user', :'pw');
  ELSE
    EXECUTE format('ALTER ROLE %I WITH LOGIN PASSWORD %L', :'app_user', :'pw');
  END IF;
END$$;
-- Grant connect on the database (use safe identifier quoting)
-- Use plain SQL expansion here because the DB name is validated/escaped above
GRANT CONNECT ON DATABASE "${POSTGRES_DB}" TO "${POSTGRES_APP_USER}";
SQL
# Run migrations via canonical runner from workspace
if [ ! -x "${WORKSPACE}/scripts/run_migrations.sh" ]; then
  echo "migration runner not found or not executable: ${WORKSPACE}/scripts/run_migrations.sh" >&2; exit 6
fi
sudo bash "${WORKSPACE}/scripts/run_migrations.sh" || { echo "run_migrations failed" >&2; exit 7; }
# Ensure schema ownership and privileges in target DB
sudo -u postgres psql -v ON_ERROR_STOP=1 -d "${POSTGRES_DB}" <<-SQL || { echo "granting privileges failed" >&2; exit 8; }
ALTER SCHEMA IF EXISTS app_schema OWNER TO "${POSTGRES_APP_USER}";
GRANT USAGE ON SCHEMA app_schema TO "${POSTGRES_APP_USER}";
GRANT ALL PRIVILEGES ON ALL TABLES IN SCHEMA app_schema TO "${POSTGRES_APP_USER}";
SQL

Waits up to 30s with backoff for readiness. Records which restart method was used or why restart was skipped. Cleans up temporary artifacts. #!/usr/bin/env bash
set -euo pipefail
WORKSPACE="/home/kavia/workspace/code-generation/pricecompare-pro-327749/postgresql_db"
BACKUP="$WORKSPACE/backup.dump"
: "${POSTGRES_APP_USER:=devuser}"
: "${POSTGRES_PASSWORD:=devpass}"
: "${POSTGRES_DB:=devdb}"
# Source secrets
if [ -f /root/.postgres_secrets ]; then source /root/.postgres_secrets; fi
# pre-checks
command -v pg_restore >/dev/null || { echo "{\"status\":\"fail\",\"reason\":\"pg_restore missing\"}" >&2; exit 2; }
pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432 >/dev/null || { echo "{\"status\":\"fail\",\"reason\":\"postgres not ready\"}" >&2; exit 3; }
PRE_READY_TS=$(date --iso-8601=seconds 2>/dev/null || date)
# Detect restart method
RESTART_METHOD="none"
if command -v systemctl >/dev/null 2>&1 && systemctl --version >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RESTART_METHOD="systemctl"
elif command -v service >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RESTART_METHOD="service"
elif command -v pg_ctlcluster >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RESTART_METHOD="pg_ctlcluster"
elif command -v pg_ctl >/dev/null 2>&1; then
  RESTART_METHOD="pg_ctl"
else
  RESTART_METHOD="none"
fi
RESTARTED=false
case "$RESTART_METHOD" in
  systemctl)
    sudo systemctl restart postgresql.service >/dev/null 2>&1 && RESTARTED=true || RESTARTED=false
    ;;
  service)
    sudo service postgresql restart >/dev/null 2>&1 && RESTARTED=true || RESTARTED=false
    ;;
  pg_ctlcluster)
    # Restart all clusters (Debian/Ubuntu packaging)
    sudo pg_ctlcluster --skip-systemctl --force 12 main restart >/dev/null 2>&1 && RESTARTED=true || RESTARTED=false || true
    ;;
  pg_ctl)
    # Attempt to find PGDATA (best-effort); skip if unknown
    if [ -n "${PGDATA:-}" ]; then sudo -u postgres pg_ctl restart -D "$PGDATA" -m fast >/dev/null 2>&1 && RESTARTED=true || RESTARTED=false; fi
    ;;
  none)
    RESTARTED=false
    ;;
esac
# wait up to 30s with backoff
for i in 0 1 2 4 8 15; do
  if pg_isready -h localhost -p 5432 >/dev/null 2>&1; then break; fi
  sleep $i
done
POST_READY_TS=$(date --iso-8601=seconds 2>/dev/null || date)
# Backup (custom format)
export PGPASSWORD="${POSTGRES_PASSWORD}"
pg_dump -h localhost -U "${POSTGRES_APP_USER}" -d "${POSTGRES_DB}" -Fc -f "$BACKUP" || { echo "{\"status\":\"fail\",\"reason\":\"pg_dump failed\"}" >&2; exit 4; }
[ -f "$BACKUP" ] || { echo "{\"status\":\"fail\",\"reason\":\"backup file missing\"}" >&2; exit 5; }
# Check pg_restore compatibility (compare versions)
DUMP_VER=$(pg_dump --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $NF}' || true)
RESTORE_VER=$(pg_restore --version 2>/dev/null | awk '{print $NF}' || true)
if [ -n "$DUMP_VER" ] && [ -n "$RESTORE_VER" ]; then
  # warn if restore older than dump
  if [ "$(printf '%s\n' "$RESTORE_VER" "$DUMP_VER" | sort -V | head -n1)" != "$RESTORE_VER" ]; then
    echo "{\"status\":\"warn\",\"reason\":\"pg_restore version may be older than pg_dump\"}" >&2
  fi
fi
# Restore to temp DB
TMP_DB="${POSTGRES_DB}_restore_tmp"
sudo -u postgres psql -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS \"$TMP_DB\";" >/dev/null || true
sudo -u postgres psql -c "CREATE DATABASE \"$TMP_DB\";" || { echo "{\"status\":\"fail\",\"reason\":\"create tmp db failed\"}" >&2; exit 6; }
sudo -u postgres pg_restore -d "$TMP_DB" "$BACKUP" >/dev/null || { sudo -u postgres psql -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS \"$TMP_DB\";" >/dev/null || true; echo "{\"status\":\"fail\",\"reason\":\"pg_restore failed\"}" >&2; exit 7; }
# verify restored DB contains app_schema
if ! sudo -u postgres psql -d "$TMP_DB" -t -A -c "SELECT schema_name FROM information_schema.schemata WHERE schema_name='app_schema';" | grep -q app_schema; then
  sudo -u postgres psql -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS \"$TMP_DB\";" >/dev/null || true
  echo "{\"status\":\"fail\",\"reason\":\"restored DB missing app_schema\"}" >&2; exit 8
fi
# cleanup
sudo -u postgres psql -c "DROP DATABASE IF EXISTS \"$TMP_DB\";" >/dev/null || true
# Evidence output
echo "{\"status\":\"ok\",\"pre_ready\":\"$PRE_READY_TS\",\"post_ready\":\"$POST_READY_TS\",\"restart_method\":\"$RESTART_METHOD\",\"restart_attempted\":$RESTARTED,\"backup_present\":$( [ -f \"$BACKUP\" ] && echo \"yes\" || echo \"no\" ) }"
